title: Common-line presentations and nonnegative powers under scalar extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with finite limits and final object, small relative to the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and sheafified tensor products and recursively associated tensor powers [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $B\to A$ be a map of commutative ring sheaves, let $C_0\to C_1$ be a map of commutative $B$-algebra sheaves, and let $T$ be an $A$-module sheaf. Put $R_i=A\otimes_B C_i$ with multiplication $(a\otimes c)(a'\otimes c')=aa'\otimes cc'$ and unit $1\otimes1$, $L_i=T\otimes_B C_i$, and let $\iota:R_0\to R_1$ be induced by $C_0\to C_1$. There are natural $R_i$-linear isomorphisms
$$i_i:T\otimes_A R_i\xrightarrow{\sim}L_i,\qquad t\otimes(a\otimes c)\longmapsto at\otimes c,$$
with inverse $t\otimes c\mapsto t\otimes(1\otimes c)$; these commute with the maps induced by $C_0\to C_1$. Set $P_i(0)=R_i$ and $P_i(n)=L_i^{\otimes_{R_i}n}$ for $n\geq1$. There are natural isomorphisms
$$b_n:P_0(n)\otimes_{R_0}R_1\xrightarrow{\sim}P_1(n)\qquad(n\geq0).$$
Here $b_0(r\otimes s)=\iota(r)s$; through $i_0,i_1$, $b_1((t\otimes r)\otimes s)=t\otimes\iota(r)s$ with inverse $t\otimes s\mapsto(t\otimes1)\otimes s$; and $b_{n+1}$ for $n\geq1$ is the canonical relative tensor comparison followed by $b_n\otimes b_1$. If $T$ is locally free of rank one, meaning $T|_U\cong A|_U$ on a covering of the final object, all $P_i(n)$ are locally free of rank one on that same covering. For a local generator $e$ of $T$, put $e_i=i_i(e\otimes1)$ and $e_i^0=1$. The maps satisfy
$$b_n((r e_0^{\otimes n})\otimes s)=\iota(r)s e_1^{\otimes n}.$$
All displayed formulas are formulas on local pure tensors in the sheafified tensor products, and commute with restrictions.

proof.text: Use the tensor construction of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The bijection of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] constructs a map out of a sheaf tensor from a restriction-compatible balanced bilinear formula and detects equality on pure tensors. For tensors over different rings, first apply the ordinary balanced tensor universal property sectionwise, then the factorization and uniqueness of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For a nested tensor, or a product of two sheafified tensors, a factor $\mathcal F^\#$ is the module sheafification of a presheaf tensor $\mathcal F$; a formula given on its presheaf sections is a bilinear map of presheaves $\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$, which extends to a bilinear map $\mathcal F^\#\times\mathcal G^\#\to\mathcal H$ by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension-existence] (with $\mathcal G=\mathcal G^\#$ when the other factor is already a sheaf), and two such extensions agreeing on presheaf sections are equal by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension-uniqueness]. The bijection above then turns the extended bilinear map into a map out of the sheaf tensor. Repeat this one factor at a time for nested tensors. Thus each formula below is a map of sheaves, and checking inverse composites or commutative diagrams on the displayed nested pure tensors suffices. No assertion that every section is globally a pure tensor is used.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: sheafified tensor definition, associativity and change-of-rings formulas, and Hom/Bilin universal property following Tag 0GMW; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback.

proof.text: Construct the stated ring and module structures using this procedure: the multiplication and the action are the bilinear extensions [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension-existence] of the sectionwise formulas on the presheaf tensors $A(V)\otimes_{B(V)}C_i(V)$ and $T(V)\otimes_{B(V)}C_i(V)$, and each identity below holds after sheafification by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension-uniqueness] once it holds on presheaf sections. For each $i$, the product on $R_i$ sends $(a\otimes c,a^{\prime}\otimes c^{\prime})$ to $aa^{\prime}\otimes cc^{\prime}$, and its action on $L_i$ sends $(a\otimes c,t\otimes d)$ to $at\otimes cd$. These formulas are additive and $B$-balanced in each original tensor: moving $b\in B$ between either pair of factors has the same image, because the $B$-actions on $A,C_i,T$ agree. Associativity, commutativity and unit for the product, and the module axioms for the action, reduce respectively to the corresponding identities in $A,C_i,T$; the unit is $1\otimes1$. The map induced by $C_0\to C_1$ preserves these formulas, so is the ring map $\iota$ and induces the compatible semilinear map $L_0\to L_1$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: sheafified tensor definition, associativity and change-of-rings formulas, and Hom/Bilin universal property following Tag 0GMW; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback.

proof.text: Define $i_i$ and $j_i$ by $i_i(t\otimes(a\otimes c))=at\otimes c$ and $j_i(t\otimes c)=t\otimes(1\otimes c)$. For $i_i$, balancing over $A$ is $(a^{\prime}t)\otimes(a\otimes c)=t\otimes(a^{\prime}a\otimes c)$, and both images are $a^{\prime}at\otimes c$; balancing over $B$ in the inner tensor is the $B$-relation in $L_i$. For $j_i$ the $B$-relation follows from $(bt)\otimes(1\otimes c)=t\otimes(b\otimes c)=t\otimes(1\otimes bc)$. Multiplication of a generator by $a^{\prime}\otimes c^{\prime}$ shows that both maps are $R_i$-linear. Their composites are the identity: $i_i j_i(t\otimes c)=t\otimes c$, while $j_i i_i(t\otimes(a\otimes c))=at\otimes(1\otimes c)=t\otimes(a\otimes c)$. The universal properties in step 1 extend these equalities to the sheaf tensors. This proves the common presentations without any local-freeness assumption.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: sheafified tensor definition, associativity and change-of-rings formulas, and Hom/Bilin universal property following Tag 0GMW; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback.

proof.text: Write $\phi:C_0\to C_1$. Both paths in the common-presentation square send $t\otimes(a\otimes c)$ to $at\otimes\phi(c)$; hence the $i_i$ commute with coefficient change. Through these presentations define $b_1$ by $((t\otimes r)\otimes s)\mapsto t\otimes\iota(r)s$ and its inverse by $t\otimes s\mapsto(t\otimes1)\otimes s$. The $A$-balance and $R_0$-balance hold because $\iota$ commutes with $A\to R_i$; both maps are $R_1$-linear. One composite fixes $t\otimes s$; the other sends $(t\otimes r)\otimes s$ to $(t\otimes1)\otimes\iota(r)s=(t\otimes r)\otimes s$. By step 1 these are inverse sheaf maps. The same formulas show naturality in $T$ and in a commuting diagram of the coefficient algebra maps.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: sheafified tensor definition, associativity and change-of-rings formulas, and Hom/Bilin universal property following Tag 0GMW; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback.

proof.text:
For degree zero set $b_0(r\otimes s)=\iota(r)s$, with inverse $s\mapsto1\otimes s$; the composites are identities by the balanced relation. For $n\geq1$, suppose $b_n$ has been constructed. Apply [lem-sp-scalar-extension-binary-coherence] to $R_0\to R_1$, $N=P_0(n)$ and $P=L_0$. Its binary isomorphism, written with the scalar on the right by commutativity, is
$$((x\otimes y)\otimes s)\longmapsto(x\otimes s)\otimes(y\otimes1).$$
Follow this with $b_n\otimes b_1$ to define $b_{n+1}$. Each constituent is an isomorphism, so this proves the claim by induction from $b_1$. It is precisely the relative tensor comparison of the statement, using the left-associated recursion of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The cited binary comparison is natural in both module factors, so induction with step 4 proves naturality of every $b_n$. The passage between left and right scalars is the symmetry of the sheaf tensor, given by swapping the two arguments of the bilinear maps of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. The right-scalar form can also be checked directly: its inverse before applying the $b$ maps sends $(x\otimes s)\otimes(y\otimes u)$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes su$; the two composites use only balancing. Thus no unspecified choice of comparison enters the recursion.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: sheafified tensor definition, associativity and change-of-rings formulas, and Hom/Bilin universal property following Tag 0GMW; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback.

proof.text: Now assume that $T|_U\cong A|_U$ on the given covering, with generator $e$ and coefficient map $q:T|_U\to A|_U$ inverse to $a\mapsto ae$. By [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction], all tensors and change-of-ring tensors above restrict to the corresponding tensors on $\mathcal C/U$, preserving their pure-tensor formulas. In this slice, step 3 identifies $L_i|_U$ with $T|_U\otimes_{A|_U}R_i|_U$. This is freely generated by $e_i=i_i(e\otimes1)$: $r\mapsto r e_i$ has inverse induced by $t\otimes s\mapsto q(t)s$. In degree zero $P_i(0)|_U=R_i|_U$. If $P_i(n)|_U$ is freely generated by $e_i^{\otimes n}$, the next tensor is freely generated by $e_i^{\otimes n}\otimes e_i$: multiplication of coefficients $(r,u)\mapsto ru$ has inverse $v\mapsto v(e_i^{\otimes n}\otimes e_i)$. Balancing proves the two composites are identities. This induction proves local freeness of rank one for every degree on the original covering itself.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: sheafified tensor definition, associativity and change-of-rings formulas, and Hom/Bilin universal property following Tag 0GMW; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback.

proof.text: Finally check the normalized generator formula. Degree zero is the definition of $b_0$. In degree one, $b_1(e_0\otimes1)=e_1$ by step 4 and $R_1$-linearity gives $b_1((r e_0)\otimes s)=\iota(r)s e_1$. Suppose the formula holds in degree $n\geq1$. The binary comparison in step 5 sends $((r e_0^{\otimes n}\otimes e_0)\otimes s)$ to $((r e_0^{\otimes n})\otimes s)\otimes(e_0\otimes1)$. Applying $b_n\otimes b_1$ gives $(\iota(r)s e_1^{\otimes n})\otimes e_1=\iota(r)s e_1^{\otimes(n+1)}$. This is the required induction. Every defining formula applies only module operations, coefficient maps and tensor formation to its input; these commute with restriction. The slice comparison of [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] preserves those same pure tensors, so the formulas and their equalities hold after any restriction.
